tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported
- `{src,test}/**/*.ts` — cartesian brace expansion is supported too

Results are capped at the first 100 matching paths. If a search would return more, a truncation marker is appended. Refine the pattern (extension, subdirectory) when 100 is not enough, or call again with a narrower anchor.

Large-directory caveat — avoid recursing into dependency / build output even with an anchor, especially when `include_ignored` is set:
- `node_modules/**/*.js`, `.venv/**/*.py`, `__pycache__/**`, `target/**` can produce thousands of results that truncate at the match cap and waste context. Prefer specific subpaths like `node_modules/react/src/**/*.js`.

path.description: Directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Defaults to the current working directory.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

include_dirs.description: Deprecated and ignored. Results are always files-only — directories are never listed. Accepted only so older calls that still pass this flag are not rejected by parameter validation.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Search file contents using regular expressions (powered by ripgrep).

Use Grep when the task is to find unknown content or unknown file locations. Do not use shell `grep` or `rg` directly; this tool applies workspace path policy, output limits, and sensitive-file filtering.
ALWAYS use Grep tool instead of running `grep` or `rg` from a shell — direct shell calls bypass workspace policy, output limits, and sensitive-file filtering.
If you already know a concrete file path and need to inspect its contents, use Read directly instead.

Write patterns in ripgrep regex syntax, which differs from POSIX `grep` syntax. For example, braces are special, so escape them as `\{` to match a literal `{`.

Hidden files (dotfiles such as `.gitlab-ci.yml` or `.eslintrc.json`) are searched by default. To also search files excluded by `.gitignore` (such as `node_modules` or build outputs), set `include_ignored` to `true`. Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always skipped for safety, even when `include_ignored` is `true`.

path.description: File or directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Omit to search the current working directory. Use Read instead when you already know a concrete file path and need its contents.

glob.description: Optional glob filter for which files to search, e.g. `*.ts`. Matched against each file's full absolute path, so a path-anchored pattern like `src/**/*.ts` silently matches nothing — use a basename pattern (`*.ts`), or anchor with `**/` (`**/src/**/*.ts`). To scope the search to a directory, use `path` instead.

type.description: Optional ripgrep file type filter, such as ts or py. Prefer this over `glob` when filtering by language or file kind: it is more efficient and less error-prone than an equivalent glob pattern.

output_mode.description: Shape of the result. `content` shows matching lines (honors `-A`, `-B`, `-C`, `-n`, and `head_limit`); `files_with_matches` shows only the paths of files that contain a match, most-recently-modified first (honors `head_limit`); `count_matches` shows per-file match counts as `path:count` lines, preceded by an aggregate total line. Defaults to `files_with_matches`.

-i.description: Perform a case-insensitive search. Defaults to false.

-n.description: Prefix each matching line with its line number. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`. Defaults to true.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`.

-C.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`; takes precedence over `-A` and `-B`.

head_limit.description: Limit output to the first N lines/entries after offset. Defaults to 250. Pass 0 for unlimited.

offset.description: Number of leading lines/entries to skip before applying `head_limit`. Use it together with `head_limit` to page through large result sets. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline matching, where the pattern can span line boundaries and `.` also matches newlines. Defaults to false.

include_ignored.description: Also search files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Read a text file from the local filesystem.

If the user provides a concrete file path to a text file, call Read directly. Do not `Glob`, `ls`, or otherwise pre-check known text file paths; missing or invalid file paths return errors you can handle. Do not use Read for directories; use `ls` via Bash for a known directory, or Glob when you need files matching a name pattern (Glob lists files only, never directories). Use `Grep` only when the task is to search for unknown content or locations.

When you need several files, prefer to read them in parallel: emit multiple `Read` calls in a single response instead of reading one file per turn.

- Relative paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute.
- Returns up to 1000 lines or 100 KB per call, whichever comes first; lines longer than 2000 chars are truncated mid-line.
- Page larger files with `line_offset` (1-based start line) and `n_lines`. Omit `n_lines` to read up to the 1000-line cap.
- Sensitive files (`.env` files, credential stores, SSH private keys, and similar secrets) are refused to protect secrets; do not attempt to read them. Templates and public keys are exempt: `.env.example` / `.env.sample` / `.env.template` and public SSH keys such as `id_rsa.pub` read normally.
- Only UTF-8 text files can be read. Non-UTF-8 encodings, binary files, and files containing NUL bytes are refused; use `ReadMediaFile` for images or video, and Bash or an MCP tool for other binary formats.
- Negative line_offset reads from the end of the file (for example, -100 reads the last 100 lines); the absolute value cannot exceed 1000.
- Output format: `<line-number>\t<content>` per line.
- A `<system>...</system>` status block is appended after the file content; it summarizes how much was read (line and byte counts, truncation, line-ending notes) and is not part of the file itself.
- Pure CRLF files are displayed with LF line endings; `Edit` matches this output and preserves CRLF when writing back.
- Mixed or lone carriage-return line endings are shown as `\r` and require exact `Edit.old_string` escapes.
- After a successful `Edit`/`Write`, do not re-read solely to prove the write landed. When the task depends on an exact file, API, or output shape, inspect the final external contract before finishing.

path.description: Path to a text file. Relative paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute. Directories are not supported; use `ls` via Bash for a known directory, or Glob for pattern search.

line_offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Omit to start at line 1. Negative values read from the end of the file; the absolute value cannot exceed 1000.

n_lines.description: The number of lines to read; the tool also applies its internal cap. Omit to read up to the internal cap of 1000 lines.

Reference binary: `/workspace/executable` (`stg`). All experiments in throwaway repos under /tmp.

## 1. Exit codes

| code | meaning | examples |
|------|---------|----------|
| 0 | success | any successful command |
| 1 | CLI parse/usage error (clap) | unknown flag, unknown subcommand, invalid value, missing option value, conflicting flags |

| 3 | merge conflict during a transaction | `push`/`goto` etc. hitting conflicts |
| 101 | Rust panic | printing `-h` help into a closed pipe (SIGPIPE); see §11 |

## 4. Color behavior

Possible values: `auto`, `always`, `ansi`, `never` (default `auto`).

**Key finding: `auto` never produced color in any tested environment** — including a real
pty (via `script` and python `pty.spawn`) with `TERM=xterm`/`TERM=xterm-256color`, with
`CLICOLOR_FORCE=1`, with `git config color.ui always`, with `git config stgit.color always`.
Only `--color always` and `--color ansi` force colors; both produce identical ANSI output.
`NO_COLOR=1` does NOT override `--color always`/`ansi` (explicit flag wins). With default
`auto`, output is always plain in practice.

### `stg series --color always` raw bytes (applied p1, topmost p2, unapplied p3):
```
^[[0m^[[32m+ ^[[0m^[[0mp1^[[0m
^[[0m^[[34m> ^[[0m^[[0m^[[1mp2^[[0m
^[[0m^[[35m- ^[[0m^[[0m^[[2mp3^[[0m
```
Line structure: `ESC[0m` + colored 2-char prefix (marker+space) + `ESC[0m` + `ESC[0m` + styled name + `ESC[0m` + `\n`.

Styles:
| marker | meaning | prefix color | name style |
|--------|---------|--------------|------------|
| `+ ` | applied (not top) | green (32) | none |
| `> ` | topmost applied | blue (34) | bold (1) |
| `- ` | unapplied | magenta (35) | dim (2) |
| `! ` | hidden | red (31) | dim+italic (2;3) |

Hidden line (`stg series --hidden --color always`):
`^[[0m^[[31m! ^[[0m^[[0m^[[2m^[[3mp3^[[0m`

With `-e/--empty`, a leading column: `*` (cyan 36, `^[[0m^[[36m*^[[0m`) for empty patches,
or a literal space for non-empty, prepended before the normal prefix:
```
^[[0m^[[36m*^[[0m^[[0m^[[32m+ ^[[0m^[[0mp1^[[0m
 ^[[0m^[[34m> ^[[0m^[[0m^[[1mp2^[[0m
```

### Transaction output (`pop`/`push`/`new`/...) uses the same scheme, on stdout:
`stg pop --color always` (pop topmost p2, new top becomes p1):
```
^[[0m^[[35m- ^[[0m^[[2mp2^[[0m
^[[0m^[[34m> ^[[0m^[[1mp1^[[0m
```
Note transaction lines differ from series: NO extra `ESC[0m` before the name style
(series: `ESC[0mESC[0mESC[1mname`; transaction: `ESC[0mESC[1mname`).

`stg push --color always`:
```
^[[0m^[[34m> ^[[0m^[[1mp2^[[0m
```

New patch line: plain `> p1 (new)`; colored: `^[[0m^[[34m> ^[[0m^[[1mp1^[[0m^[[0m^[[33m (new)^[[0m` — annotations like ` (new)`, ` (empty)`, ` (conflict)` are yellow (33).

### Conflict output (`stg push --color always`, conflict) — exit 3:
stdout:
```
^[[0m^[[31m> ^[[0m^[[1mc2^[[0m^[[0m^[[33m (conflict)
UU f.txt
^[[0m
```
- topmost marker is RED (31) instead of blue when the push ends in conflict
- after the transaction lines, the git status-ish conflict list (`UU f.txt`) is printed to stdout, followed by a final `ESC[0m`
stderr:
```
^[[0m^[[1m^[[31merror: ^[[0mmerge conflicts; resolve conflicts manually then refresh or undo the operation with `^[[0m^[[33mstg undo --hard^[[0m`.
```
(plain text: `error: merge conflicts; resolve conflicts manually then refresh or undo the operation with `stg undo --hard`.`)

## 5. Environment variables

- `GIT_DIR` honored: `GIT_DIR=/path/repo/.git stg series` works from anywhere.
- `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL` honored by `new` (commit author changes).
- `GIT_EDITOR` honored (see §8).
- `STGIT_AUTHOR`: **no observable effect**.
- `STGIT_DEBUG=1`: no observable effect.
- `STGIT_COLOR`: no observable effect (`STGIT_COLOR=always` piped → still plain; `STGIT_COLOR=bogus` silently ignored, exit 0).
- `NO_COLOR`: respected in theory per help text ("The `NO_COLOR` environment variable is
  respected"), but since `auto` never colorizes anyway there is no observable difference;
  does NOT override explicit `--color always`/`ansi`.
- `TERM=dumb` with `--color ansi` still colors (flag is unconditional).

## 6. git config knobs (`stgit.*`)

- `stgit.autosign`: WORKS. `git config stgit.autosign "Signed-off-by"` then
  `stg new -m m p` → commit message becomes `m\n\nSigned-off-by: Test <t@t.com>\n`.
  With a plain word: `bogus` → trailer `bogus: Test <t@t.com>`.
  Quirk/bug: if the value already contains a full `Key: Value`, e.g.
  `Signed-off-by: Auto Signer <auto@example.com>`, the trailer is rendered as
  `Signed-off-by: Auto Signer <auto@example.com>=Test <t@t.com>` (literal `=` + committer
  ident appended).
- `stgit.pick` = `name`: no observable effect, no error.
- `stgit.bogusknob`: silently ignored, no error. Unknown `stgit.*` keys are never validated.
- `color.ui`, `stgit.color`: no effect on stg colorization.

## 7. Repository-state-dependent behavior

- Not a git repo: exit 2, `error: Could not find a git repository in '.' or in any of its parents`
  (same for `series` and `init`).
- Repo with zero commits (unborn HEAD): exit 2, `error: branch `refs/heads/master` is unborn`
  (for `init`, `series`, `new` alike).
- Detached HEAD: exit 2, `error: not on branch, HEAD is detached` (for `init`, `series`, `new`).
- Bare repo WITH commits: works fine — `stg series` exit 0 (empty), `stg init` exit 0.
  (Bare repo without commits → same "unborn" error as above.)
- Linked worktree (`git worktree add`): works; stacks live in the common refs namespace
  (`refs/stacks/<branch>`), one stack per branch.
- Subdirectory of repo: all commands work from any subdir. `stg files <patch>` prints
  **repo-root-relative** paths regardless of cwd (e.g. `A sub/file2.txt` even from inside
  `sub/deep`). The editor tempfile `.stgit-edit.txt` is created in the **cwd** (observed
  `CWD=/tmp/exp_tmpl/sub FILE=.stgit-edit.txt`) and removed after a successful edit.
- Stack auto-initialization: most commands DO NOT auto-init... except state-changing ones:
  in a fresh repo with no `refs/stacks/master`, `stg series` → exit 0, empty output, no ref
  created; `stg new -m x p1` → succeeds and creates the stack silently (same `> p1 (new)`
  output as if initialized). `stg series -b <branch-without-stack>` → exit 0, empty output.
- `stg init` on initialized branch: exit 2, `error: StGit stack already initialized for branch `master``
- `stg init -b other` works while checked out on `master`; creates `refs/stacks/other`.
  Fresh stack.json content (note: 2-space indent, no trailing newline):
  ```json
  {
    "version": 5,
    "prev": null,
    "head": "<head-commit-sha>",
    "applied": [],
    "unapplied": [],
    "hidden": [],
    "patches": {}
  }
  ```
- Corrupt stack ref (refs/stacks/master pointing at a blob): exit 2,
  `error: Object named <sha> was supposed to be of kind commit, but was kind blob.`
- Dirty worktree blocking transaction (`stg pop sp` with modified file): exit 2,
  stderr `error: worktree not clean; use `refresh` or `reset --hard``, no stdout.
- `stg push` with nothing to push: exit 2, `error: no unapplied patches`.
- `stg pop` / `stg pop --all` / `stg top` with nothing applied: exit 2, `error: no patches applied`.
- `stg push nosuchpatch` / `stg goto nosuchpatch`: exit 2, `error: patch `nosuchpatch` does not exist`.
- `stg undo` with no history: exit 2, `error: not enough undo information available`.
- `stg id nosuchpatch`: exit 2 `error: patch `nosuchpatch` does not exist`;
  `stg id nosuchbranch:tp3`: exit 2 `error: branch `nosuchbranch` not found`;
  `stg id -b nosuch`: exit 2 `error: branch `nosuch` not found`.

## 8. Editor & message templates (`stg new`, `stg edit`)

- Editor command resolution: `GIT_EDITOR` env honored; falling back to `vi` (observed when
  no editor configured: `error: running editor: vi: No such file or directory (os error 2)`,
  exit 2). Before invoking, stderr gets: `hint: Waiting for your editor to close the file...`
- Failing editor (`GIT_EDITOR=false`): exit 2, stderr:
  ```
  hint: Waiting for your editor to close the file...
  error: problem with the editor `false`
  ```
- Editor temp file: `.stgit-edit.txt`, created in the CURRENT working directory (even in a
  subdirectory), deleted after success. Exact initial content for `stg new tp3`:
  ```
  Patch:  tp3
  Author: Test <t@t.com>
  Date:   2026-08-07 12:12:47 +0000
  
  
  
  # Please enter the message for your patch. Lines starting with
  # '#' will be ignored. An empty message aborts the new patch.
  # The patch name and author information may also be modified.
  ```
  (Date format `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS +0000`; `stg edit` uses the SAME template text —
  it still says "aborts the new patch".)
- Template file: `.git/patchdescr.tmpl` (i.e. `$GIT_DIR/patchdescr.tmpl`). If present, its
  content pre-fills the message area of the editor file. With `GIT_EDITOR=true` (no-op) the
  template becomes the verbatim commit message. `.stgit-new.txt` in the worktree root or in
  `.git/` is NOT read (no effect).
- Despite the comment, an EMPTY message does NOT abort: `GIT_EDITOR=true stg new tp1`
  succeeds with an empty commit message; `GIT_EDITOR=true stg new` (no name) creates a patch
  auto-named `patch`.
- `--save-template <file>` writes the would-be editor content (template above) to FILE
  (`-` = stdout) and exits 0 without creating the patch. Conflicts with `-m` (clap error, §2).
- Auto-generated patch names: when no name given, derived from first line of `-m` message;
  duplicates get `-1`, `-2`, ... suffixes (`msg`, `msg-1`, ...). Empty message → `patch`.

## 9. Patch name validation (`stg new <name>`)

Validation failures are clap value errors: exit 1, format
`error: invalid value '<name>' for '[patchname]': invalid patch name `<name>`: <reason>`
followed by blank line + `For more information, try '--help'.`

Exact reasons observed:
| name | reason |
|------|--------|
| `with space`, `tab\tname` | `patch name may not contain whitespace` |
| `slash/name` | `patch name may not contain '/'` |
| `a..b` | `patch name may not contain '..'` |
| `.lead` | `patch name may not start with '.'` |
| `trailing.` | `patch name may not end with '.'` |
| `a.lock` | `patch name may not end with '.lock'` |
| `tilde~x` | `patch name may not contain '~'` |
| `caret^x` | `patch name may not contain '^'` |
| `colon:x` | `patch name may not contain ':'` |
| `quest?x` | `patch name may not contain '?'` |
| `star*x` | `patch name may not contain '*'` |
| `brack[x` | `patch name may not contain '['` |
| `back\slash` | `patch name may not contain '\'` |
| `at@{x` | `patch name may not contain '@{'` |
| `` (empty) | `patch name may not be empty` |
| `a\x01b` (control char) | `patch name may not contain control characters` |

ACCEPTED names (exit 0): `-dash` (leading dash, when passed after `--` or alone), `-`
(single dash), `at@`, `héllo-wörld`, `日本語`, names containing a literal newline,
300-char and 1000-char names pass VALIDATION but then fail at ref-creation time with
exit 2 and a two-line stderr:
```
error: An IO error occurred while applying an edit: File name too long (os error 36);
command aborted (all changes rolled back)
```
Names equal to existing branch names (`master`, `topic`) are ACCEPTED (no collision check).
Duplicate patch name: exit 2, `error: patch `at@` already exists`.

From `stg new --help`: "The given patch name must be unique in the stack. If no name is
given, one is generated from the first line of the patch's commit message. Patch names
follow the rules for Git references with the additional constraint that patch names may
not contain the '/' character."

Note: everything after `--` is a PATHSPEC, not a name: `stg new -m msg -- weirdname` treats
`weirdname` as a path limiter and auto-generates the patch name from the message.

## 10. `stg id` formats

- `stg id` (no args): full 40-char sha1 of the topmost applied patch commit. Exit 0.
- `stg id <patch>`: sha of that patch's commit. `stg id <patch>^`: parent commit.
- `stg id '{base}'`: sha of the stack base commit.
- `stg id <branch>:<patch>`: patch on another (initialized) branch.
- Accepts plain git revspecs too (`master`, `HEAD`, ...).
- Errors: see §7 (exit 2).
